title: The Lord Our God Is Full of Might
description: The Lord Our God Is Full of Might in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Kirke White wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 573, “In a Storm”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord our God is full of might, The winds o-bey His will; He speaks, and in His heav-enly height The roll-ing sun stands still.

lines: The Lord our God is full of might,
He speaks, and in His heavenly height
Rebel, ye waves! and o'er the land
The Lord uplifts His awful hand,
And chains you to the shore.
Howl, winds of night! your force combine;
Ye shall not in the mountain pine
Ye nations bend, in reverence bend;
And bid the choral song ascend

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Kirke White died in 1806.
credits: Words by Henry Kirke White (1785–1806), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
